title: ScreenConnect one-time password failures
volume: None to a few a week, from technicians who mistype a code. Several for one account in a short time means someone else has its password.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: One custom detection rule for ConnectWise ScreenConnect, on the Auth records the library's ScreenConnect parsers write from its security automation. It makes a detection when a sign-in gives the right password and a wrong one-time password. It matches sensor type ConnectWise ScreenConnect only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's ScreenConnect parsers and send the automations in its README through bridges/webhook-relay, which adds the HTTP Ingest key, then run the check-your-data search to see events arrive.
- The security automation's event filter needs LoginAttempt.

How it works:
- ScreenConnect logs the result OneTimePasswordInvalid when the password was right and the one-time password wrong, and the parsers write it with failure category INCORRECT_MFA, which the rule takes.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-23, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 7 records agreed. The samples went in with their dates moved to the day before the test, so they fell inside the search's time range.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines within about two minutes.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on the lines these rules take. Sophos's sign-in analytics flagged only a sample sign-in that succeeded, as an unseen user, address or application.
- The lines went through bridges/webhook-relay, run on the lab machine, as text/plain, the way ScreenConnect's Perform Web Request sends them.

Known gaps:
- Sign-ins through an external identity provider check MFA there, not in ScreenConnect, so they make none.
- Password failures and lockouts aren't taken: Sophos's own sign-in detections cover those.
